No actions this turn. The overall build hasn't been laid out yet, only how recordings get cleaned up, so that comes before the write-up.

---

Before I write it up, there's one bigger choice: where the guide lives and how volunteers get recordings into it. You've been talking about outcomes, so I'll take this one unless you'd rather weigh in. I see three ways:

1. **Add the guide to your existing website, with audio stored in the site's own files.** Each exhibit gets a page like `harbourmuseum.org/guide/42`, and the code beside the exhibit opens it. Volunteers upload through a ready-made editing tool that sits on top of the site. The cleanup runs each time the site rebuilds. This needs the fewest new parts. But those editing tools are awkward on a phone, and every replaced recording stays in the site's history forever, which makes it heavy over time.

2. **Add the guide pages to your existing website, but store the audio separately, behind a simple upload page we build.** The pages and codes work the same as in (1). A volunteer opens an upload page on their phone, picks the exhibit and the language, and attaches the recording. It's cleaned up and live a few minutes later. This means building and looking after a little more, but the upload is designed for exactly what your volunteers do.

3. **Use a paid audio-guide service.** There's nothing to build, but you'd pay every month, and Welsh support and automatic cleanup depend on the provider.

**I'll go with (2).** Volunteers uploading from their phones without help is the part most likely to fail, and (2) is the only option built around it. It also keeps the guide on your own site, where you already host and pay for things.

This is a project, so it gets a full written design. A reviewer will read it first, and I may come back once with a few questions. Tell me now if you'd prefer another option.
